findings.title: RepoTools accepts an unvalidated commit and passes it to git as an argument
findings.why: The constructor stores `commit` without checking that it is a 40-hex SHA. `search_code` and `git_log` pass `self._commit` as a standalone git argument, so a value beginning with `--` is parsed as a git option (e.g. `git grep --open-files-in-pager=...` can execute a command, `git log --output=...` can write a file). `MirrorStore.sync` validates commits, but `RepoTools` does not enforce that invariant, so any caller forwarding webhook/PR data without going through sync is exposed.

findings.title: Agent-controlled path/pattern with NUL crashes the tool
findings.why: `_clean_path` does not reject NUL, and `search_code` also passes an agent-supplied pattern to subprocess without rejecting NUL. Python's subprocess raises `ValueError: embedded null byte` before git runs; `ToolBudget.wrap` only catches `ToolError`, so the agent's tool call aborts instead of returning an error string. Reject control/NUL bytes before building git arguments.

findings.title: search_code can bypass skip rules via quoted git grep paths
findings.why: `git grep` quotes unusual pathnames by default (`core.quotePath`). The code extracts text before the first colon as `path` and compares that raw text against skip globs. For a file under a skipped directory whose name contains a non-ASCII/control/quote character, the parsed path includes quotes/escapes and does not match `is_skipped` (or `path_glob`), so matching lines from a skipped file are returned. Use `git grep -z` and parse NUL-delimited, verbatim paths before filtering.

findings.title: search_code buffers unbounded output and ignores MAX_FILE_BYTES
findings.why: `run_git` uses `capture_output=True` on `git grep`, so the entire match set is read into memory before `MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES` is applied. It also searches every text file regardless of `MAX_FILE_BYTES`, contrary to the stated 200 KB limit. A large repository or a file with a very long matching line can exhaust memory/agent context.

findings.title: ToolBudget check-and-increment is racy
findings.why: The limit check and `self.used += 1` are separate operations without a lock. If an agent invokes tools concurrently, two calls can both observe `used < limit` and both execute, exceeding the 25-call budget. Use an atomic counter or lock.

findings.title: list_dir returns an unbounded number of entries
findings.why: There is no cap on the number of entries or output size. A repository with a very large directory can produce a massive response, exhausting memory or the agent context; the other tools have per-call limits, but this one does not.

findings.title: Agent-supplied path_glob can cause catastrophic regex backtracking and cache growth
findings.why: `_glob_regex` translates `**` to `.*` and is decorated with unbounded `@cache`. A path_glob supplied by the agent (prompt-injectable) can compile to overlapping `.*` sequences that backtrack exponentially on long paths, and every distinct pattern is retained forever. Limit pattern length/use a safe glob implementation, and bound the cache.

findings.title: read_issue does not handle non-JSON API responses
findings.why: `json.load(response)` can raise `json.JSONDecodeError` or `UnicodeDecodeError` (for example, a proxy/rate-limit/HTML response). Those exceptions are not caught, and `ToolBudget.wrap` only catches `ToolError`, so the tool call crashes instead of returning an error string.

findings.title: git fetch has no timeout
findings.why: `run_git` runs `git fetch` with no timeout. A stalled network or malicious/unresponsive remote can block the review process indefinitely; `read_issue` already uses a 10-second timeout, but mirror sync does not.
